description:
After spending more than a decade “chronically online,” Gabriela Nguyen realized her struggle with distraction, anxiety, and disconnection wasn’t a personal failing—it was the product of technologies designed to hijack attention. In this candid, research-grounded talk, she introduces “appstinence,” a way of reclaiming focus and meaning by redesigning our physical, digital, and social environments. This talk offers a hopeful blueprint for building a fuller, more human life beyond addictive technology. Gabriela Nguyen is the 24-year-old founder of Appstinence, a global movement challenging the idea that social media is necessary for connection. Rather than promoting digital detoxes or moderation, Appstinence advocates complete freedom from personal social media accounts in favor of direct communication through calling and texting.

A Gen Z native of Silicon Valley, Gabriela spent a decade chronically online while growing increasingly disconnected. Her shift to being “appstinent” reveale
title: I quit social media–here’s what happened | Gabriela Nguyen | TEDxManhattanBeach

description: In her talk, Gabriela speaks about metamorphosis — the process through which we become who we truly are. She uses the metamorphosis of a butterfly as one of life’s most powerful metaphors, reflecting on the stages of change that are often difficult to understand and, at times, painful. Gabriela explores the idea that within the cocoon of vulnerability, where we may feel fragile, inner strength is quietly formed. Drawing from her personal and professional experiences, she shares how vulnerability is not a weakness, but a source of courage and authenticity. Courage, she believes, is what allows us to enter into dialogue with fear and to open our wings toward our uniqueness. Through this talk, Gabriela invites the audience to remember that we can become anything, but that every transformation begins with vulnerability, courage, and authenticity. This, she says, is the essence of true human metamorphosis. Gabriela is a change strategist and leadership coach with international experience i
title: Puterea metamorfozei umane | Gabriela Elena Blaga | TEDxCopou Women

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk explores the spark that ignites when someone underestimates you and the strength it takes to keep going when self-doubt never fully disappears. From being underestimated as a woman in engineering to leading teams in a leading AI research institute, Vanessa reveals a hard-earned, often invisible power that many women carry.
We often equate leadership with volume, dominance, and unwavering confidence but what if we’ve been measuring the wrong things? Through her journey of stepping into leadership before feeling ready, Vanessa shows how soft power—listening, empathy and collaboration—can become a true source of authority. By pairing soft power with a quiet “watch me” spark, she discovers that confidence isn’t about being the loudest in the room, but about trusting the impact you’re already having. This is a call to every woman who has questioned her place: you don’t need to feel ready to be capable. You belong and the world needs your leadership. Vanessa Parli is Managing Dire
title: Redefining confidence and leadership | Vanessa Parli | TEDxLosAltosWomen

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk shares a deeply personal journey of rebuilding life after sudden loss, uncertainty, and financial hardship. Through honest reflection and lived experience, the speaker explores how self-belief, clarity of purpose, and everyday courage can help a person stand back up when everything feels like it has fallen apart.
Rather than offering textbook motivation, the message comes from real turning points — knowing your worth, cutting the tethers, never giving up , and standing for your rights . It is a reminder that resilience is not a trait you are born with, but a choice you make repeatedly.
This is a conversation about starting over, growing stronger through adversity, and becoming, step by step, the unbeatable version of yourself. Shippy Sharma is the Managing Director at Earthling Consumer Products pvt. Ltd. She leads end-to-end business operations, product development, supply chain optimisation, sales and market expansion, and overall brand strategy, with a focus on innovation
title: The unbeatable you | Shippy Sharma | TEDxKIIT World School Youth

description:
In this talk, veterinarian and animal welfare advocate Emma Stratulat shares the powerful story behind Save Our Paws and the realities of animal suffering she could no longer ignore. Through real-life rescue experiences, Emma speaks about compassion in action, responsible adoption, and why prevention — especially sterilization — is the only humane solution to stop suffering.
Her message is simple and urgent: we may not save them all, but we can choose to act, and in doing so, change lives — and mentalities. Emma Stratulat is a veterinarian and the founder of the Save Our Paws Association. Over the years, she has learned that real change starts with small actions: saving one animal, treating a life with dignity, and choosing empathy over indifference.

She believes that every living being deserves safety and respect, and that veterinary medicine goes beyond treatment — it is also about education, prevention, and care for life in all its forms.

What if the next global economy runs without banks, borders, or permission? Blockchain, powered by data engineering and AI, is building an autonomous economic infrastructure where trust is cryptographic and value flows instantly across the world. This talk reveals why understanding this shift determines who holds power in the economy ahead. Ravi Kant designs systems that decide how intelligence is created, trusted, and acted upon. A data engineer with seven years of experience, he builds cloud platforms on AWS and Azure that transform fragmented information into strategic insight.
He is building IQ.ai under Cortex Lab, exploring how data engineering, AI, and blockchain shape next-generation decision systems. His venture has been recognised by Santander and reached the final round of a competitive incubation programme.

Passei anos atrás da câmara a fugir das atenções.
Depois percebi que não era invisível, faltava-me era "mudar a perspetiva". 

O ‘Factor X’ dos introvertidos não é falar mais alto, é colocar emoção na mensagem. 
Quando trazemos de dentro para fora o que sentimos, deixamos o rótulo e ganhamos presença. 

Esta talk mostra como transformar nervosismo em impacto, com humor, histórias reais e coração. Tiago Gonçalves, é empreendedor, comunicador e fundador da Partícula Influente, um estúdio especializado na criação de conteúdos em vídeo, cursos, podcasts e transmissões ao vivo.

Ao longo dos anos, consolidou a sua carreira na área audiovisual, começando com a cobertura de eventos sociais e corporativos, fotografia de produto e produção de vídeos promocionais.

Formou-se em áreas ligadas ao desenvolvimento pessoal, coaching, comunicação e programação neurolinguística.

title: O Factor X dos Introvertidos | Tiago Gonçalves | TEDxBraga

Discover how intentional media leadership can preserve cultural identity, influence generations, and drive meaningful transformation. Speaking with clarity and courage, she invites adults to imagine a future fifty years from now where children can enjoy cleaner seas and a healthier planet. Her message is simple and powerful: the choices we make today will shape the world young people inherit tomorrow. From his childhood to his professional experiences, he reveals how food became a powerful way to bring people together, strengthen families, and build community. He also challenges modern food trends by reminding us that practices such as organic eating, reducing waste, and using every part of an ingredient have long been a natural way of life for many cultures. José Afonso is a General Manager with a deep belief that food is far more than nourishment. It is culture, identity, and connection. Having had the honour of serving Her Late Majesty Queen Elizabeth II on multiple occasions, he brings both experience and perspective to the table. Passionate about food education, José encourages a renewed appreciation for the abundance many enjoy and invites us to reflect on how food trends shape the way we live. description:
What if the illusions we chase are not deceptions but visions waiting to find their path?

In this engaging and personal talk, Aayushi Dholakia shares her journey from a young pageant dreamer to becoming a Miss India runner-up and eventually carving an unexpected career in sports broadcasting. Through stories of vision boards, societal expectations, and career detours, she reveals how life often takes us on routes we never planned but exactly where we need to grow.

Her story challenges the notion of a fixed definition of success and encourages audiences to question the “obvious” choices the world presents to them. This talk serves as a reminder that illusion is not the destination; it is the journey that unfolds when we take action, remain authentic, and trust our own path. Aayushi Dholakia is a Miss India runner-up, sports presenter, entrepreneur, and digital creator. description:
From a curious 13 year old experimenting in her mother’s kitchen to representing India on international culinary stages and judging MasterChef, Nikitha Umesha’s journey challenges the illusions society creates about success.

In this inspiring talk, she shares how she chose passion over conventional expectations, faced a male dominated industry, left a stable corporate job, and built her entrepreneurial venture from her home kitchen. Through her story, she explores how the illusions we are told to believe about careers, creativity, and success can be questioned, reshaped, and transformed into reality.

This talk is a powerful reminder to challenge societal norms, trust your instincts, and become the architect of your own path. Nikitha Umesha is a chef, entrepreneur, and culinary innovator known for transforming her passion for food into a thriving professional journey. description: This talk explores music not as performance, but as something far more fundamental to being human. Through personal memories, shared cultural moments, and surprising science, the speaker reveals how music shapes identity, memory, and emotional resilience. Framed through the metaphor of “roots and wings,” the talk shows how songs ground us in who we are—while also giving us the courage to grow, heal, and transcend boundaries. It’s an invitation to reconnect with the music that once shaped us, and to rediscover the quiet power of finding our voice in a noisy world. Mr. Sunil Koshy is an award-winning singer, composer, vocal coach, and academician. He is the co-founder of From Mug To Mike, a platform for amateur singers, founded with his wife Archana Hallikeri. Sunil has collaborated with musical legends like Hariharan, KS Chithra, and Kumar Sanu, and has sung and composed for films, jingles, and dance dramas. title: The Flight of Sound :A journey through melody  | Sunil Koshy | TEDxClaret College Bangalore

description:
Why do people with less talent sometimes move ahead faster than those who are more capable? The answer often lies in one simple habit: showing up.

In this relatable and honest talk, the speaker explores how consistency, participation, and the courage to try—despite fear, self-doubt, or judgment—can completely change the direction of a person’s life. Through real-life moments, failures, and small victories, the talk highlights how opportunities often come not to the most talented but to the most persistent.

This talk is a reminder that success is rarely about perfection. It is about starting, continuing, and refusing to quit,even when no one is watching. Abhash Chandra Jha is a digital creator and poet known for his relatable storytelling, spoken word performances, and honest reflections on everyday struggles. By combining real-world examples, technical insight into how large language models work, and the broader societal consequences of unchecked AI adoption, he highlights why preserving truth in the age of AI has become an urgent responsibility.  Chigozie is a junior at NCSSM who enjoys volunteering at the "A Time for Science" Museum, competing in Model United Nations, and playing both the Viola and Piano. He's considering a career in Chemical Engineering and Political Science. He also hopes to further his interests in the Research in Chemistry Program at NCSSM. title: “The Death of Truth: How AI Is Warping Reality” | Chigozie Obi | TEDxYouth@NCSSM

He is drawn to exploring the complexities of human nature, particularly the moral gray areas where loyalty, survival, and power challenge simple ideas of right and wrong. Alongside his writing and speaking, Tony is deeply committed to social impact and has helped lead fundraising and water initiatives supporting rural communities along the Nile, experiences that have shaped his belief that the world is rarely as simple as it appears. He has also written a novel centered on moral ambiguity and human motivation and hopes to pursue a future as both an author and an engineer-turned-entrepreneur, creating ideas and projects that challenge how people think. Dr. Christina Grant is the Executive Director of the Center for Education Policy Research at Harvard University. Throughout her career as an educator, administrator, and executive in some of America’s largest school systems, Dr. Grant has focused on data-driven leadership and strategic management to improve student outcomes and drive academic acceleration.

At CEPR, Dr. Grant unites researchers, practitioners, and policymakers to build transformative partnerships that are grounded in rigorous research, benefiting learners at every stage of life. Her leadership emphasizes the importance of evidence-based solutions in shaping effective educational policies.

description: This talk dives deep into the importance of identity and a name. It explores how culture survives distance and time. Saia Taesali is a graduate of Moreau Catholic High School’s Class of 2025 and is currently in his first year at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.  Born and raised in the San Francisco Bay Area, Saia is of Chamorro and Samoan heritage.  Growing up thousands of miles away from his home islands, he has experienced the challenge of navigating what it means to carry his Chamorro and Samoan identity while living far from island shores. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

This is a rare look inside the principles and practices that fuel decades of sustained innovation.

description: In this talk, the speaker explores how unresolved experiences from our past continue to shape our present through a powerful Zen parable about letting go. Using the story of two monks at a riverbank, the talk illustrates how emotional burdens—such as trauma, inherited narratives, regret, and unfulfilled dreams—are often carried far longer than necessary. Drawing on personal experiences of generational trauma, migration, bullying, and perfectionism, the speaker shows how these unseen weights manifest as anxiety, fear, and self-judgment. The talk reframes mindfulness not as a trend, but as a way of living rooted in awareness, presence, and self-compassion. Through practical reflections on comparison, emotional boundaries, time pressure, and the choice between fear and faith, the speaker invites the audience to question what they are still carrying. title: Finding our true selves through mindfulness | Kassandra Fineberg | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker examines the urgent relationship between human activity, carbon emissions, and forests, beginning with a striking fact about how much CO₂ is produced by everyday actions such as driving and flying. Using accessible data and historical context, the talk traces the dramatic rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide over the last 150 years and explains why this trend poses a serious threat to life on Earth. The speaker highlights forests as a critical solution—not only for carbon absorption, but for regulating climate, providing water, food, and supporting human health. Drawing on the work of My Forest Armenia, the talk reframes reforestation as a social as well as environmental effort, emphasizing its role in job creation and quality of life, especially in rural areas. Ultimately, the talk challenges audiences to rethink humanity’s relationship with nature, recognize forests as essential to survival, and take responsibility for protecting and restoring them for future
title: The challenges of large-scale reforestation | André Gumuchdjian | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker reflects on absence, pain, and the search for life purpose, challenging the idea that purpose is something we find or achieve. Through poetic storytelling, they explore how unresolved wounds, silence, and longing shape identity over time. Central to the talk is a memory of the speaker’s grandmother and her mango tree, which becomes a metaphor for growth, patience, and healing. The speaker suggests that, like fruit, purpose does not emerge quickly or easily, but grows slowly through hardship, reflection, and survival. They examine how striving for perfection and external validation can lead to performing identities that protect rather than reflect who we truly are. Ultimately, the talk reframes purpose as something that whispers rather than roars—an authentic calling formed at the intersection of our deepest pains and passions. The audience is invited to reflect inward, embrace patience, and allow their lived experiences to shape a more honest and meaningful f
title: Finding Meaning Through Pain, Patience, and Reflection | Amevi Kwidama | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker challenges the idea that history and knowledge are neutral by examining how a single dominant narrative shapes what we learn and remember. Beginning with familiar mathematical theorems, they reveal how many discoveries credited to Western figures were developed centuries earlier in civilizations such as Babylon, ancient Egypt, India, and the Arab world. This pattern of misattribution, the speaker argues, reflects a deeper historical bias that privileges Western perspectives while erasing others. Drawing on Edward Said’s concept of Orientalism, the talk explores how these narratives have shaped modern perceptions of the East as inferior or dependent. Through personal reflection on Armenian identity, the speaker highlights how internalised bias influences how societies see themselves. The talk concludes by urging the audience to question what they think they know, recognise the power behind historical storytelling, and embrace fuller, more inclusive narratives
title: Beyond the West: The Forgotten Voices of History | Anelia Mkrtchyan | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

description: In this talk, the speaker challenges assumptions about youth, success, and emotional maturity by exploring how the brain influences decision-making at different stages of life. Beginning with a personal story of rejection—from not being selected for UWC alongside his twin—the speaker reflects on how failure and emotional setbacks can become turning points rather than endpoints. Drawing on basic neuroscience, he contrasts the adolescent brain, driven largely by emotion, with the adult brain, which prioritizes rational thinking and long-term planning. Using examples of young entrepreneurs and well-known companies founded early in life, the talk questions the idea that success must come later with age. The speaker argues that learning to manage emotions, create balance between impulse and reason, and make intentional decisions is key to achieving goals early. title: 3 Million dollar company | Hanwa Mate Ongalo | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, Daniel Barbosa explores how everyday decisions—rather than luck—shape our future selves. He begins by reflecting on our uncertainty about the future and introduces the idea that destiny is built through small, repeated actions. Using a personal story from his experience competing in tennis, Daniel shows how shifting focus from winning to improving individual skills transformed both his performance and mindset. He then examines the hidden power of subconscious decision-making, referencing research that shows most of our choices happen automatically. Through a relatable example involving eating chocolate while working, he illustrates how seemingly minor habits can accumulate into significant long-term consequences. To counter this, Daniel proposes a simple three-question framework to evaluate decisions and encourages reflective practices such as journaling to build awareness. title: How Everyday Decisions Shape Who We Become | Daniel Barbosa | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this talk, the speaker explores the future of education in a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence. Imagining a classroom in 2035 where AI handles lesson planning, assessment, and administrative tasks, the speaker challenges the fear that teachers will become obsolete. Instead, they argue that AI has the potential to make educators more essential than ever. By reducing workload, AI could create space for what technology cannot replicate: slow, meaningful, human-centered conversations. Drawing on observations from teaching and reflections on modern communication, the talk distinguishes dialogue from transactional question-and-answer exchanges. The speaker emphasizes the importance of conversations about values, belonging, community, and purpose—discussions that require time, trust, and presence rather than efficiency. title: Today We Need Teachers More Than Ever Before | Milan Miljkovic | TEDxUWCDilijan Youth

Drawing on personal experiences growing up in Armenia and later studying in the United States, she challenges the idea that security is tied to geography or fixed destinations. Through moments of loss, displacement, and unexpected change, the speaker explains how uncertainty is an inevitable part of life and how meaning comes from embracing the journey rather than controlling its outcome. She introduces a practical framework built around defining core values, regularly reflecting on one’s path, and practicing gratitude. The talk encourages the audience to become the “pilot” of their own life—making decisions guided by values rather than fear. Ultimately, it reframes success as the ability to stay grounded, flexible, and purposeful while navigating life’s many destinations.
